subject.title: 2026.7.1 gateway crash-loop: legacy memory sidecar `meta`/`chunks` conflicts are fatal while `files` conflicts auto-resolve

question: When legacy Memory Core `meta` or `chunks` rows conflict with the canonical per-agent index, what proof is sufficient to discard or archive the legacy copy without risking unique memory data?
rationale: The outage is clearly reproducible, but choosing canonical-wins for every table changes the persisted-data preservation contract; source inspection alone cannot determine whether divergent chunk content may be discarded.

options.title: Use table-specific convergence
options.body: Treat compatible cache and derived metadata as canonical-wins, while requiring positive supersession or merge proof before archiving divergent chunks.

options.title: Keep every conflict fail-closed
options.body: Preserve the current data-safety policy but add a guided Doctor repair that shows the conflict and lets the operator archive or reconcile it without manual file work.

options.title: Make canonical rows authoritative
options.body: Archive the entire legacy sidecar whenever the canonical index is non-empty, accepting that unique divergent legacy chunks may be discarded.

recommendation.title: Use table-specific convergence
recommendation.body: Treat compatible cache and derived metadata as canonical-wins, while requiring positive supersession or merge proof before archiving divergent chunks.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and co-authored the original persisted-state migration and have the strongest visible ownership signal for the Memory Core upgrade contract.
